A proportional table uses one fixed multiplier from input x to output y. Today we find that multiplier and complete missing values.
For every row with nonzero input, divide y by x. All ratios must equal the same k. If input is zero, output must be zero.
For pairs (2,6), (4,12), and (7,21), the ratios are all three. So the table follows y equals three x.
If (3,12) and (5,?) are proportional, k is four and the missing output is twenty.
If k is three point five and y is twenty-four point five, divide to find x equals seven.
The first two pairs (2,6) and (4,12) give k three. For x six, the output must be eighteen, not nineteen.
Enter (1,3), (2,6), and (4,12) into a Desmos table, then enter y equals three x. The points lie on the line through the origin.
Check constant ratios, handle zero rows separately, and use y equals k x. A constant difference alone does not prove proportionality.
